title: High-Nuclearity Lanthanide-Containing Clusters as Potential Molecular Magnetic Coolers
claim: Hydrothermal or solvothermal conditions let simple carboxylates, which precipitate with lanthanides under ambient pressure before hydrolysis, dissolve enough to support slow ligand-controlled hydrolysis and growth of giant clusters.
explanation: The authors analogize this limited solubility to slow crystallization: gradual assembly favors larger clusters over smaller analogues and expands the ligand set beyond those usable at ambient pressure. Acetate is highlighted because its small mass can also raise magnetic density, as in Gd24Zn4 and the Ln104 (Ln = Gd, Nd) clusters.
scope: Lanthanide and 3d–4f hydroxide clusters supported by simple carboxylates such as acetate, propionate, nicotinate, chloroacetate, and benzoate.
conditions: Hydro/solvothermal synthesis; hydrolysis-limiting carboxylate ligands whose lanthanide salts are poorly soluble at ambient pressure.
caveats: Assembly remains sensitive to ligand/metal ratio, pH, temperature, and time; nuclearity above 25 is still uncommon.
evidence_locations: Conspectus; Section 2 opening; Section 2.1; Figures 2–3; refs 18, 20–25
